feedback: Based only on iteration 1 (sensors at y=0.06, five sensors at x=±0.03 m, wheel_radius 0.03, wheel_track 0.10, kp 3.2, ki 0.15, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.6). All 60 trials ended off_track. Progress was 0.11 to 0.15, max_error was at the 0.06 m floor on every track, and rms_error was about 0.025 m. Line loss averaged about 1 per run, and steering_oscillation stayed low (0.10 to 0.14). Iteration 1 improved the s-bend progress from 0.04 to 0.15 over iteration 0, but the robot still drifts outward. What I had to compensate for in the controller: the weights are scaled to the new lateral spread to keep the signal sign-correct, the kp is raised for turn authority, and kd is raised to damp the faster response. Next race, the change depends on the result. If max_error still reaches 0.06 m on the s-bend with seven sensors at y=0.07, the bend is still being seen too late or the turn is still too slow, so try sensor y=0.08 (the contract maximum). If line_loss_events stay at about 1 per run with the seven-sensor array, the 0.012 m footprint may be too small to hold the tape at the edges, so try sensor_size 0.016. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.16 with the wider track, the turn response is too slow to damp, so return wheel_track toward 0.10 m. I expect the completion risk to come from the speed limit, not the sensing.
requested_changes: If max_error stays at about 0.06 m on the s-bend with the seven-sensor array at y=0.07: move sensor y to 0.08 m (the contract maximum), keeping x at -0.03 to +0.03 m, since iteration 1 showed the robot still drifting outward at y=0.06 m.

If line_loss_events remain at about 1 per run (iteration 1: 1.0 on oval and s-bend, 2.0 on slalom in iteration 0): set sensor_size to 0.016 so each footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape and the edge sensors keep a usable reading.

If steering_oscillation rises above the iteration 1 range (0.10 to 0.14) with wheel_track 0.11 m: return wheel_track to 0.10 m, since iteration 1 ran at 0.10 m with low oscillation and the same max_error floor.
